title: Channel partner bundle strategy + marketplace readiness checklist (sketch)
content:
Purpose:

This is a working sketch for a channel-focused bundle strategy that maps Redwood’s hosted API and Dedicated capacity offerings into partner-ready products for cloud marketplaces and reseller channels. Intent: create 2–3 simple SKU bundles per partner type, define onboarding entitlements, marketplace listing copy variants, and a preflight checklist to accelerate partner submission and reduce back-and-forth with marketplace review teams.

Audience:
- GTM partnerships and alliance managers
- Marketplace program managers
- Solutions/SEs preparing buyer-facing collateral
- Legal and finance for contract/SKU alignment

Status notes (quick):
- Draft, high-level pricing bands only. Needs finance validation for margins and VAT rules per region.
- Engineering/Infra needs to confirm Dedicated isolation language and SLA guarantees for bundled offers.
- Legal: data residency & customer data processing text TBD for EU/UK marketplaces.

1) Target partner segments and bundle types (short):
- ISV Co-sell Bundle (for SaaS ISVs who embed Redwood inference): includes sandbox hosted credits + integration SDK support hours + optional Dedicated trial.
- MSP Managed Inference Bundle (for managed service providers): includes Dedicated capacity slot reservation, higher onboarding professional services, and monitoring/observability add-on credits.
- Reseller Starter Pack (for cloud resellers and VARs): basic hosted API credits, marketing co-op funds, joint listing asset package.

2) Proposed SKU matrix (sketch, not final):
- RWD-ISV-START: 50K hosted-tokens + 5 evals + 4 SDK hours (30-day) — price band: $2.5–3.5k
- RWD-ISV-PLUS: 250K hosted-tokens + 25 evals + 12 SDK hours + 14-day Dedicated trial — price band: $9–12k
- RWD-MSP-BASIC: 1 Dedicated-slot (shared pool) reservation for 30 days + 100K hosted-tokens + onboarding PS 20h — price band: $25–35k
- RWD-RESELLER-CORE: 100K hosted-tokens + marketplace listing asset pack + 1 co-marketing fund credit — price band: $4–6k
Notes: token counts are illustrative. We should align to typical customer usage profiles (support/assistant, summary, embeddings). Finance must validate floors and discounting for marketplace promos.

3) Onboarding & entitlements (what partner customer gets immediately):
- Auto-provisioned account with trial credits and role-based access (Admin + SE).
- Walkthrough playbook per SKU (short doc link to be created) and 1 onboarding SE session for ISV-PLUS / MSP packages.
- For Dedicated trials: short-term capacity reservation, clear SLA snippet, eviction/fallback behavior documented.

4) Marketplace listing copy variants (short vs long vs bullet) — copy drafts to iterate:
Short headline (30 chars max): "Low-latency LLM inference — flexible bundles"
Short description (1 line): "Redwood Inference: predictable LLM serving for apps — hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with enterprise-ready controls."
Long description (marketing): "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLMs in production with consistent latency, cost, and reliability. Choose hosted API for fast integration, reserved Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for regulated workloads. This partner bundle combines onboarding credits, integration support, and optional Dedicated trials to reduce time-to-value. Ideal for ISVs embedding LLM features, MSPs offering managed AI, and resellers packaging AI capabilities for customers."
Feature bullets (for marketplace UI sections):
- Production-grade inference runtime: batching, KV caching, and quantization support
- Model catalog & version pinning with rollout controls
- Dedicated capacity options with SLA-backed latency targets
- Observability: token-level cost + per-route latency dashboards
- Flexible deployment: hosted, dedicated, private (VPC/on-prem)
Compliance blurbs (short): "SOC 2, ISO 27001 posture; enterprise compliance add-ons available."

5) Acceptance checklist for marketplace submission (preflight):
- Product metadata completed: logo (1200x627), 1–3 screenshots, 30/120/250 char descriptions.
- SKU definitions uploaded: machine-readable SKU ids + pricing tiers + region availability.
- Billing integration validated: marketplace invoice flow + partner margins documented.
- Legal: Acceptable Use Policy snippet + Data Processing Agreement (DPA) link + Export control check.
- Technical: Onboarding automation flow implemented (provisioning API + email welcome template).
- Security: Contact for security review included + SOC 2 cert snapshot (or attestation).
- Marketing: One-pager asset + joint webinar outline + co-marketing credit code ready.
- Co-sell/go-to-market: Partner enablement deck + SE playbook + closed-loop lead routing (jira/slack integration).

6) Operational playbook: who owns what during a partner review cycle
- GTM Partnerships (owner): partner negotiation, pricing, SLA exceptions, co-marketing plan
- Marketplace Program Manager (owner): listing submission, asset QA, region gating
- Finance (owner): SKU mapping, partner margining, billing reconciliation spec
- Legal (owner): DPA, reseller addendum, IP language for partner-resold usage
- Engineering (owner): provisioning API, Dedicated trial gating, metric/usage telemetry hooks
- Solutions/SEs (owner): partner onboarding runbook, 1st-month enablement sessions

7) Rejection risk flags and mitigation notes (from prior experiences):
- Too-broad claims on security/compliance: keep cert language conservative and link to compliance page.
- Missing SKU granularity: marketplaces frequently reject when pricing matrix is ambiguous — include per-region SKUs if pricing varies.
- Billing flow mismatch: ensure marketplace invoice / payout timing aligns with Redwood revenue recognition expectations.
- Trial abuse: put quota/time limits and automated abuse-detection hooks.

8) Copy variants for partner-specific pitching (short snippets for partner pages/emails):
- For ISVs: "Embed Redwood to serve LLMs with predictable cost and latency — SDKs, example templates, and a dedicated trial to validate performance at scale."
- For MSPs: "Offer managed inference as a service on top of Redwood — reserved capacity, telemetry, and SLAs to run your customers' LLM workloads."
- For Resellers: "Bundle Redwood credits and go-to-market assets — start selling AI-powered features to existing accounts with minimal integration work."

9) Open questions / TODOs:
- (Engineering) Confirm exact Dedicated trial mechanics: how is capacity reserved and billed if trial converts? ticket: GTM-8721
- (Finance) Validate price bands and discount ladder for Marketplace promos and co-sell incentives
- (Legal) Draft reseller addendum language and DPA snippet for listings
- (GTM) Create a small set of localized descriptions for EU/JP marketplaces
- (Marketing) Generate three screenshot variants focusing on console, latency dashboard, and a sample integration snippet

10) Next steps (immediate 2-week sprint):
- Finalize SKU ids and get finance sign-off (owner: Maya)
- Prototype provisioning flow for marketplace auto-provision (owner: Arjun)
- Draft final marketplace long description + screenshot set (owner: Liam)
- Book legal review for reseller addendum (owner: Priya)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep bundle matrix intentionally simple: marketplaces like low-friction, easily billable SKUs.
- Be explicit about fallback behavior when Dedicated capacity is exhausted — reviewer teams always ask this.
- Consider a single trial SKU that can be consumed either as hosted credits or as a Dedicated trial to reduce listing complexity.

Appendix (links/refs):
- Example partner listing that worked well on AWS: aws-case-ref-Redwood-sample (internal link to be added)
- Internal audit: previous marketplace rejections log (confluence:marketplace-rejections-2024)

End of sketch.
